text:
Peter DeBoer's first full season on Long Island has a split personality. The Islanders are 8-6-4 with 20 points, which looks like a team hanging around. The chances say they've been outplayed: 45.6% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against), and they have allowed about 12 fewer goals than those chances predicted. That is the goalies' doing. Semyon Varlamov has saved 5.0 goals above expected over his last five starts, even with a 1-2-1 record to show for it.

Matthew Schaefer remains the reason to watch. He has 11 points in his last ten games against 10.0 expected, so this is no hot streak, and a headline this week had him tying Bobby Orr in NHL history. Rookie Victor Eklund (8 points in 10, 4.7 expected) is running hotter than his chances; Sharks forward Mason Marchment was fined for roughing him. The line of Brayden Schenn, Emil Heineman and Eklund has outscored opponents 8-1, while Bo Horvat's line with Kyle Palmieri and Simon Holmstrom creates the most but gives plenty back.

Help is arriving. Ryan Pulock and Matias Maccelli returned against the Kings on Thursday, a 5-2 win in which captain Horvat reached 18 points to match Schaefer, and Mathew Barzal travelled with the team on this trip. Our numbers give the Islanders a 22% chance at the playoffs. The process has to catch up with the goaltending.
headline: Goaltending and a teenage star keep Islanders afloat
